newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan to mourn Versace in memorial mass.
newsitem.headline: Milan to mourn Versace in memorial mass.

text.p: A memorial mass will be held for murdered fashion king Gianni Versace next Tuesday at Milan's main Roman Catholic cathedral, his brother and sister said in a statement on Saturday.

The statement by Santo and Donatella Versace thanked "all those who have shared with admiration and love the beautiful years of Gianni's creativity and who have taken part in this painful and absurd ending".
It said the mass would begin at six p.m. local time inside Milan's central Duomo, which is just a stone's throw from Versace's atelier and the workshops of the city's other top fashion designers.
Versace, 50, was shot dead outside his Miami Beach mansion on Tuesday by a lone gunman as he returned home from buying magazines.
Police have mounted a massive manhunt for 27-year-old Andrew Cunanan, a homosexual prostitute and alleged "spree killer" whom they describe as their only suspect.

Santo, the business brains behind the multi-million dollar Versace empire, and Donatella, a talented designer and creator of the house's Versus line, returned to Italy on Friday from Miami with their brother's ashes.
They were laid to rest in a secluded cemetery in the northern village of Moltrasio where the fashion designer had lived in an 18th century neo-classical villa on Lake Como for the past 10 years.

Local residents said he used his aristocratic Villa Fontanelle as a retreat or a place to entertain some of his jet-set friends, including supermodel Naomi Campbell, pop stars Madonna and Bruce Springsteen and actor Sylvester Stallone.
Versace was born in the poor southern city of Reggio Calabria where he learnt his trade from his seamstress mother.

He launched his first collection under his own name at the age of 31 and developed a reputation for brash, sexy clothes in building a business empire that had a total revenue from all brands of 1.705 trillion lire ($975 million) in 1996. ($1=1,748)
